title: Provide feedback about progress of failed Suspend/Sleep job
line: When Sleep or Hibernate fails, Plasma now shows a notification with the reason instead of doing nothing.
explanation: Every Sleep/Hibernate button (launcher, logout screen, power button via PowerDevil) ends in libkworkspace's LogindSessionBackend, which called logind and threw away the reply. When logind refused, for example with "There's already a shutdown or sleep operation in progress" as in the report, or because of a blocking inhibitor, nothing visible happened. Now a failed reply shows an error notification ("Could not go to sleep" / "Could not hibernate") with logind's message, except when the user cancelled authentication. A quit lock keeps short-lived callers such as the logout screen alive until the notification has been sent.

commits.message:
libkworkspace: show a notification when going to sleep fails

When logind refused to sleep, for example because an earlier request was
still in progress, nothing visible happened. Now a notification shows
the error from logind, unless the user cancelled authentication.

BUG: 483107

media.caption: Master: Sleep clicked in the launcher while logind refuses (sleep already in progress); nothing happens
Fixed: the same click shows "Could not go to sleep" with logind's reason
Master: Sleep clicked on the logout screen; the screen closes and nothing tells you it failed
Fixed: the logout screen closes and the notification still appears

reviews.text: Pragmatic fix in the right central layer (libkworkspace's LogindSessionBackend) that surfaces systemd-logind errors for Suspend, HybridSleep, Hibernate, and SuspendThenHibernate via a standard KNotification error event instead of silently discarding the D-Bus reply. Suppressing AccessDenied and InteractiveAuthorizationRequired avoids spurious errors on cancelled polkit prompts, and holding a QEventLoopLocker until notification destruction properly prevents short-lived callers like ksmserver-logout-greeter from dropping the notification on exit. The dbusmock tests and screenshots clearly prove both Kickoff and logout-greeter paths as well as regression cases.
